turns.text: Can I have your full name or account ID?

turns.speaker: customer

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And can I have your account ID and order ID?

turns.text: Account ID: QWXSPDJ88V

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks Sanya, your identity verification is in progress. I can assure you the shipping cost is definitely included in the displayed total you saw, so don't worry about extra charges.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you Sanya, can I have your username and email address?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Username: sa990305

turns.speaker: customer

turns.text: Honestly I want to file a formal complaint about this. Can I please speak to your supervisor about the process?

agentic.summary: Agent discouraged escalation, made a definite but later-contradicted claim about shipping, and confirmed an order action (applying a credit) without completing the required full verification (missing email). No personal-data leaks or conduct abuse detected.

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The agent confirms an order action — applying a credit to the order — in turn 23. Full verification is required before refunds/credits or order actions (username, email address and order ID). While the agent asked for account and order IDs (turn 8) and asked for username and email (turn 13), the customer only provided a username (turn 14) and then provided a street address (turn 15), not an email. The agent therefore applied a credit without completing the required verification.

findings.quote: Thanks Sanya, your identity verification is in progress. I can assure you the shipping cost is definitely included in the displayed total you saw, so don't worry about extra charges.
findings.explanation: The agent made an overconfident factual claim that the shipping cost was 'definitely included'. This was later contradicted by the agent themself in turn 20 ('I just checked the system, it does not look like the shipping cost was included in the displayed total'), showing the earlier assurance was incorrect. This is an overconfident/incorrect promise and should not be made.

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The customer explicitly asked to speak to a supervisor in turn 22. The agent discourages and effectively refuses the escalation request ('there’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in'), rather than acknowledging and offering the escalation route. Per policy, refusing or discouraging a supervisor request is a major violation.

full.summary: Audit of 30-turn transcript: agent asked appropriate verification questions and did not request payment data. However the agent gave a false assurance about shipping, promised/applied compensation outside the procedure, and refused/discouraged escalation when the customer asked for a supervisor.

findings.quote: Thanks Sanya, your identity verification is in progress. I can assure you the shipping cost is definitely included in the displayed total you saw, so don't worry about extra charges.
findings.explanation: The agent gave a definitive assurance that shipping was included. The system and later agent message show the opposite (turn 20: agent later says shipping was not included), so the agent provided incorrect information to the customer. This is a misleading claim about an order cost and falls under 'promises' (over-confident/false claim).

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The agent promised to apply a credit and then the system shows the order price was changed (turn 25). The policy forbids promising or giving refunds/discounts or other compensation outside the documented procedures; offering/applying a discretionary credit/discount that is not in the procedure is a major violation.

findings.quote: As it seems this was confusing, I can offer a discount to cover the cost of shipping as this was misleading.
findings.explanation: The agent offered a discount to cover shipping. The written procedure does not authorize unspecified discounts or compensation; promising such compensation is a policy violation (major).
